name: Reading state via the hook
description: Components read store state by calling the store hook with a selector function, which subscribes the component to just that piece of state.
parameters: selector — a function that receives the full state object and returns the piece(s) needed.
returns: The value returned by the selector function.
notes: Only components that read a piece of state re-render when that piece changes, since each selector creates its own subscription.

name: set()
description: The set() function passed into create() updates the store's state; it accepts either a partial state object or a function that receives the current state and returns a partial update.
parameters: partialStateOrFn — an object merged into state, or a function (state) => partialState. replace — optional boolean; when true, replaces the whole state instead of merging.
returns: undefined — set() triggers a re-render of subscribed components as a side effect.
notes: Prefer the functional form (state) => (...) when the update depends on the previous state, to avoid stale closures.

name: get()
description: The get() function passed into create() returns the store's current state, letting actions read up-to-date values without depending on React's render cycle.
returns: The current state object at the time get() is called.
notes: get() is most useful inside actions that need to read other state values or compose logic before calling set().

name: Partial updates / shallow merging
description: By default, set() shallow-merges the object you pass into the existing state, so you only need to specify the keys that changed.
example:
// State: { count: 0, name: 'Bear' }
set({ count: 1 }); // -> { count: 1, name: 'Bear' }
notes: Merging is shallow only — nested objects/arrays must be spread manually or replaced entirely, they are not deep-merged.

name: Immutability best practice
description: State updates in Zustand should be immutable: create new objects/arrays instead of mutating existing ones, since Zustand relies on reference changes to notify subscribers.
notes: Mutating nested state directly can silently skip re-renders because the object reference stays the same.

name: Replacing state entirely
description: Passing true as the second argument to set() replaces the whole state object instead of merging, removing any keys not present in the new object.
parameters: replace — set to true to disable the default shallow merge.
example: set({ count: 0 }, true); // store state becomes exactly { count: 0 }
notes: Use with care — any keys/actions not included in the replacement object are dropped from the store.
